content: Why is it impossible to eliminate half of an unsorted array like we do in Binary Search?
expectedEvidence: Because without sorting, any element could be anywhere, so no range can be safely excluded.

content: Given an array, how would you systematically guarantee you find the target if it exists?
expectedEvidence: Start at index 0 and check every element until the end.

content: Write a Java method to perform a linear search returning the index.
expectedEvidence: for loop from 0 to length-1, checking arr[i] == target.

content: Provide a counterexample where an early exit fails.
expectedEvidence: Target at the end of the array.

content: Given an array of temperatures, find if there is any day where the temperature strictly dropped compared to the previous day. How would you solve this in one pass?
expectedEvidence: Use a linear scan, comparing arr[i] with arr[i-1] starting from index 1. Return true as soon as arr[i] < arr[i-1].

content: How would you use a linear scan to find the maximum element in an unsorted array, and why does this require checking every single element instead of exiting early?
expectedEvidence: Maintain a max_seen variable. It requires checking every element because the maximum could be at the very last position, unlike searching for a specific target where you can stop once found.
